---
title: "Add speaker metadata"
date: 2026-11-14
---

Use the Python GPUI metadata manager to edit `datas/measurements/<speaker>/meta.toml`.
The manager previews TOML and validates each save with the Rust generator.
It preserves comments on unchanged fields and rejects overwriting files that
changed outside the editor.

## Install and start the manager

Install Python 3.12 and the private measurements submodule in an authorized checkout.
The native host supports macOS, Windows, and Linux with glibc 2.39 or newer.
No Rust toolchain is needed for the UI. Saving requires the Rust validator built below.
From the repository root, install the UI dependencies and build the validator:

```{.shell}
python3.12 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
make metaedit
```

To open an existing speaker directly:

```{.shell}
make metaedit SPEAKER="Brand Model"
```

You can also start the module with `PYTHONPATH=src`:

```{.shell}
python -m metaedit.app --speaker "Brand Model"
```

The catalogue path defaults to this checkout's `datas/measurements` directory.
Use `--metadata-dir /path/to/measurements` for another catalogue, with its
`origins.toml` file in the parent directory. Use `--generate-graph /path/to/generate-graph`
to select another validator binary. `SPINORAMA_GENERATE_GRAPH` also sets that path.

The native GPUI shell provides the theme picker. The Python UI uses the
`gpui-toolkit` 0.11.x package from PyPI and its bundled native host.

## Add or edit a speaker

1. On **Select speaker**, select an existing entry or enter a
   brand and model for a new entry. Click **Next**.
2. On **Edit metadata**, set the type, shape, price, and optional amount.
   Leave unknown optional fields empty. The name of an existing speaker stays
   tied to its measurement directory. Rename that directory and its metadata
   separately before reopening the editor.
3. Add at least one measurement. Give each measurement a unique version key,
   select its format, and enter an origin registered in `datas/origins.toml`.
4. Fill in reviews, notes, and optional data-acquisition details, extras, and
   specifications. The mean-band fields set `parameters.mean_min` and
   `parameters.mean_max` in Hz. Enter both values together.
5. Use **Edit measurement** to switch between versions. Select the default measurement.
   For metadata without measurement files,
   select **Skip generation (metadata only)**. Otherwise, prepare the files
   under `datas/measurements/<speaker>/<version>/` before saving.
6. Click **Review TOML**. Use **Show diff** for an existing entry
   or **Copy TOML** to copy the preview.
7. Click **Save metadata**. The manager validates a staged copy before replacing
   the speaker's `meta.toml` file. Fix any reported errors and save again.

**Choose picture…** copies an image into `datas/pictures` using the speaker's
brand and model as its filename. Picture paths are separate from the TOML metadata.

Commit metadata changes in the measurements submodule. Commit pictures and the
updated submodule pointer in the main repository. The editor saves locally;
use your normal Git workflow to review and publish the changes.

## Add measurement files or an origin

Register a new origin's plot limits, URL, and optional logo in
`datas/origins.toml`. Use that exact origin name in the measurement metadata.
For SPL/HV text, store a separate horizontal or vertical file for each angle
under `datas/measurements/<speaker>/<version>/`.

The editor records metadata. Use the appropriate importer to prepare GLL or
Klippel files. For graph-only sources, follow
[the digitization tutorial](03_digitalisation.qmd).

Validate metadata and measurement files before generating the website:

```{.shell}
make check-meta
make check-meta-files SPEAKER="Brand Model"
make images SPEAKER="Brand Model"
```

Images are written below `dist/speakers/<speaker>/<origin>/<version>/`.
Private graph payloads are written below `dist-private/speakers/`.

## Test the editor

Run the model, GPUI session, and native-validator save tests with:

```{.shell}
make test-metaedit
```

Save tests use temporary catalogues and leave the measurements submodule unchanged.
